builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Why Speculative Decoding Works Better Than Predicted on Sparse MoE Models
summary: Speculative decoding replaces standard one-token-per-forward-pass autoregressive decoding by drafting multiple tokens with a small model and verifying them in a single target-model pass, and this work refines the cost model for MoE targets. It requires maintaining a draft model alongside the target, adds verification and routing-analysis complexity, and its measured benefit on MoE models depends on kernel bandwidth utilization and expert routing overlap that vary by hardware. It can fail to deliver expected speedups when the draft model's acceptance rate is low, when the target model is dense rather than sparse MoE, or when GPU execution dynamics differ from the H100 profiling used in the paper.
rationale: Speculative decoding is deployable on a single 24 GB GPU through existing inference stacks, but the paper's revised gains apply specifically to large sparse MoE models whose size exceeds single-GPU constraints, so the practical benefit depends on whether the reader serves such models via quantization or APIs.
technique: Speculative decoding for sparse MoE inference

Higher speculative decoding speedup at low batch sizes on recent fine-grained sparse MoE models than prior predictions; the IPF model predicts unique expert counts with less than 4% error, but the abstract gives no absolute end-to-end speedup number.
